questions.q: Why is clicking via JavaScript risky in tests?
options: It bypasses real user checks like visibility and overlays, hiding bugs
questions.explain: Use it only as a diagnosed workaround.

questions.q: What does arguments[0] refer to in execute_script?

questions.q: What does the Navigation Timing API give you?
Why is browser-based performance testing noisy?
options: Variability in machine, network and scheduling
questions.explain: Use dedicated tools for load testing.

questions.q: What can Chrome DevTools Protocol add in Selenium 4?

questions.q: What should a CI run of Selenium tests do on failure?

questions.q: Why pin browser and driver versions in CI?
questions.explain: Use containers or Selenium Manager with pinned versions.

questions.q: How do you keep CI Selenium suites fast?

questions.q: Where should secrets for test accounts live in CI?
What is a notable advantage of Playwright over Selenium?

What decides which tool to use?

questions.q: What is the sleep antipattern?

questions.q: Why is time.sleep(5) after a click a poor fix for a flaky test?
options: It is either too short (still flaky) or too long (slow) and never checks the real condition
questions.explain: Wait for the condition the next step needs.

questions.q: A test passes alone but fails in the full suite. What is the likeliest cause?
options: Shared state or ordering dependence between tests
questions.explain: Make each test create and clean its own data.

questions.q: Why keep locators in page objects rather than in tests?
options: A UI change needs one edit instead of changing every test
questions.explain: Tests state intent; pages know the UI.

questions.q: Why not keep WebElement objects as long-lived page-object fields?
options: They go stale when the DOM re-renders; store locators and look up on use

questions.q: What does driver.quit() do that close() does not?
options: Ends the whole session and driver process, closing all windows

questions.q: Why avoid mixing implicit and explicit waits?
options: Their timeouts can combine unpredictably, making failures slow and confusing

questions.q: Which locator is usually the most stable?
options: A dedicated id or data-testid attribute
questions.explain: Agree stable test hooks with developers.

questions.q: How do you handle a JavaScript confirm() dialog?
options: click the OK button in the DOM
questions.explain: Alerts are not part of the DOM.

questions.q: How do you reach into an open shadow root?
options: element.shadow_root, then find elements within it
questions.explain: Normal lookups cannot cross the boundary.

questions.q: What do you pass to a file input to upload a file?
options: send_keys with the file's absolute path
questions.explain: Do not automate the native dialog.

questions.q: What does Selenium Grid add?
options: Parallel sessions across machines and browsers behind one endpoint

questions.q: Why capture screenshots and page source on failure?
options: Without them CI failures are hard to diagnose after the browser is gone

questions.q: What is the honest use of automatic test retries?
options: A temporary measure while tracking and fixing the root cause

questions.q: Which test is best pushed down from the UI to an API or unit test?
options: Business-rule logic with many input combinations
questions.explain: UI tests are slow; keep them for journeys.

challenges.title: A page object with a synchronised search
challenges.prompt: Build a ShopPage page object for a small search page whose results appear 400 ms after you click Search. Locators live in the class, search() waits for the status text instead of sleeping, and tests only call page methods. This runs against real headless Chrome with Selenium, on a local data: page that this exercise provides.
challenges.explain: The click sets the status to 'loading' immediately, so waiting for 'done' with an explicit wait is race-free. Locators as (By, value) tuples work with both find_element(*loc) and expected conditions. Verified by running it with Selenium 4 and headless Chrome.

challenges.title: A resilient custom wait
challenges.prompt: Write wait_until, a helper that polls a condition, tolerates stale-element errors during re-renders and raises a clear TimeoutException with context. Use it to wait for a toast and for a list to reach three items after an asynchronous re-render.
challenges.expected:
first went stale
['one', 'two', 'three']
timeout: nine items
challenges.explain: Selenium's own WebDriverWait does the same job; writing it once shows the mechanics: poll, swallow expected transient errors, and explain the timeout. The re-render replaces the list, so the original element goes stale. Verified by running it with Selenium 4 and headless Chrome.
